newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Oct 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Oct 15.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- GAS KEPT WAITING ON TERMS OF INQUIRY

British Gas is still waiting to find out if it will face a full-blown Monopolies Commission investigation into all its activities. The gas industry regulator, Clare Spottiswoode, had asked the commission to look at price controls for TransCo, the pipeline subsidiary and the biggest profit earner for British Gas, but said it may be possible for the terms of the investigation to be widened.
-- GEORGE TELLS CLARKE TO KEEP LID ON BORROWING

The governor of the Bank of England, Eddie George, has sent a letter to Kenneth Clarke, the chancellor, in the hope of persuading him to use next month's budget to cut the public sector deficit rather than to offer pre-election tax cuts. Mr George fears that if the level of public borrowing are not reduced to a more sustainable level, the chancellor is risking a financial backlash.
-- US GROUP MAY SELL STAKE IN WESSEX

U.S. haulage and rubbish disposal group, WMX Technologies is considering the disposal of its 20 per cent stake in Wessex Water. The disposal of its 50.7 million shares worth 175 million stg at current market prices could not take place until early 1998 and would have to be approved by Wessex Water.
THE TIMES
-- BROKERS FINED OVER PENSIONS MIS-SELLING

The Investment Management Regulatory Organisation handed down fines totalling 405,000 stg yesterday on four of the UK's largest financial broking houses. The watchdog found that the firms failed to provide some of their investors with fair and clear written statements when they transferred out of occupational and company pension schemes into personal plans.
-- SLUGGISH MARKETS HOLD BACK PREMIER

Premier Farnell, the electronic components distributor, is unable to move forward due to sluggish markets. With 410 million stg of debt, the company had slower growth in sales this year despite strong demand for computer chips. Prices in the group's volume distribution business have fallen because of overcapacity. Premier Farnell's first-half pre-tax profits were held back to 56.1 million stg.
-- GERMAN SHOE CHAIN COULD REIGNITE HINCHLIFFE CAREER

Stephen Hinchliffe is using a German shoe retailing chain to fund a possible return to the business arena after the Sheffield businessman's Facia empire collapsed. The collapse of Facia is currently being investigated by the Serious Fraud Office. Mr Hinchliffe managed to keep Bata Schuhe, the German arm of the empire, out of the hands of the receiver.
THE GUARDIAN
-- BARINGS CHIEF CLAIMS HALF A MILLION STG BONUS

An industrial tribunal yesterday heard that the boss of jailed Barings Bank trader Nick Leeson was offered a 500,000 stg bonus just one day before the institution collapsed. The new owners then refused to pay the bonus to Mary Walz who was the global head of equity financial products, and then dismissed her. Ms Walz is now seeking to have the payment restored.
-- VAUXHALL'S 300 MILLION STG INVESTMENT GIVES HOPE TO ELLESMERE PORT

Vauxhall will announce a 300 million stg investment in its Ellesmere Port car plant this morning. The investment represents a massive vote of confidence in the factory by General Motors, Vauxhall's parent company. The money will be spent over three years to modernise and reorganise assembly operations, and to make a new version of the Astra car and light van.
-- FOUNDERS OF PRISM RAIL IN 27 MILLION STG SHARES BONANZA

Seven founder investors in Prism Rail are now sitting on shares worth 27 million stg after launching a rights issue last night. The investors who already owned 5 million of Prism's 13 million shares were awarded another 1.83 million shares after the company took over its latest two franchises, South Wales and West Railway and Cardiff Railway.
-- STATISTICS POINT TO STEADY GROWTH AND LOW INFLATION

The latest economic statistics paint a picture of low inflation and steady, sustainable growth. The figures suggest that Chancellor Kenneth Clark will be able to ignore pressure from the Bank of England to raise the cost of borrowing. Underlying inflation at the factory gate was at its lowest since 1967 last month, and the pound is at its highest level against the mark for almost two years.
-- BA AND VIRGIN CHASE BANKRUPT FRENCH AIRLINE

British Airways and Virgin Express have announced separate bids for the bankrupt French airline, Air Liberte. The two will face tough competition from two French companies and a Government that would prefer a French solution for the airline coveted for its strong position at Paris's Orly airport.
